messages:
jordan_acme: Hi team — during our POC today the streaming responses from the Redwood API are frequently dropping mid-response. Client sees partial JSON and then a parse error. very intermittent, ~30% of streams.

alex_ae: thanks for flagging, jordan. can you paste an example of the truncated chunk or the client error stack? also which SDK / browser / runtime?

jordan_acme: attaching a tiny snippet we captured from the browser console: 
`SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input`
and server SSE raw-ish payload (truncated):
```
data: {"id":"msg_1","delta":"Hello, wor

```
we're using the rjs client in an electron app (node 18).

maya_se: ok — 2 quick checks: 1) try curl with -N to reproduce raw SSE and see if server cuts stream: `curl -v -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=redwood-large\"` 2) check proxies between client and Redwood — nginx/CloudFront often buffer chunked responses and close after a timeout.

chris_runtime: also confirm if responses are gzipped. streaming + gzip + some proxies = chunk boundary issues. if you can share the request_id we can correlate in logs.

jordan_acme: request-id: `req_20260320_9ab3`
Here is the raw tcp dump around the close (sanitized):
```
...
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Connection: keep-alive
...
000a
data: {"id":"msg_1","delta":"Hello, wor
0000 (connection closed)
```

sara_support: got it — filing a ticket and pulling logs now. quick theory: Nginx proxy_read_timeout or proxy_buffering closing before client finishes parsing. also check client-side SSE parser — electron's net/http stack sometimes buffers until EOF.

chris_runtime: looking at our edge logs for req_20260320_9ab3 — I see `upstream prematurely closed connection` around the same time. We had a small patch to the streaming muxer rolled out earlier today. deploy-bot: `deploy v2.14.1 to runtime` succeeded at 1766003000.
\
deploy-bot: deploy v2.14.1 -> runtime completed by ci/cd (users: maya_se).

maya_se: two immediate mitigations we can try: 1) server-side keepalive pings in SSE (send `:\n` comment pings every 10s) so intermediaries don't idle-timeout, 2) if proxies require buffering disabled: nginx needs `proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 3600;` on the upstream location.

jordan_acme: we pushed `proxy_buffering off` on the nginx side and re-ran the client. so far one full stream arrived successfully. will run more load.

chris_runtime: thanks — I'm also going to roll back the streaming muxer patch to test. if rollback fixes it we'll revert the change and cut a patch. meanwhile, can you confirm if you're hitting any 429s? partial streams sometimes happen when the process hits a soft rate-limit and kills the connection.

jordan_acme: no 429s seen in the client. just abrupt closes.

sara_support: created ticket S-2329 and scheduled a 30m deep-dive with eng-runtime + you (jordan) in 30m. next actions: jordan to run 3 full POC sessions with proxy_buffering off and collect two request_ids for failures; maya/chris to test rollback and share build. I'll attach correlation logs to the ticket.

maya_se: extra parsing tip for your client while we triage: don't expect single-line JSON per event. accumulate `data:` lines and only JSON.parse when the event end is reached (SSE delim is a blank line). if using the SDK, update to latest patch that includes incremental reassembly helpers.

jordan_acme: got it — i'll collect more req ids and try `curl -N` repro as well. thanks all. :thumbsup:

sara_support: noted. reopening here once we have two failing req_ids or a repro. will keep the ticket moving. :white_check_mark:
